blocks.title: Wetlands—the kidneys of the planet
blocks.body: Wetlands include mangroves, peatlands, rivers, lakes, deltas, seagrass beds, and coral reefs across climates and continents. Protecting and restoring them is central to a net-zero, nature-positive future.

blocks.title: Explore world wetlands from your screen
blocks.body: Major wetland areas cluster in high latitudes and tropical forests. Asia holds about 31.8% of global wetland area, North America about 27.1%. China’s wetlands total roughly 56.35 million hectares—first in Asia.

blocks.title: Wetlands around me: Shanghai’s wetland mosaic
blocks.body: Shanghai has 13 wetland areas totaling about 6,335 km²; nearly half of the land area connects to wetlands. Chongming Dongtan, Jiuduansha, and Dianshanhu form a ladder from internationally important sites to urban nature.
